limits: Lists the files it is given or the project holds; there is no server-side run store, so a stateless door lists only what its caller passes.
bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Reads sealed run files' bookkeeping; every verdict it reports was computed by run_discovery_programme.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which research runs are there, and what state is each in?

description: List research runs without running anything: the runs this project holds (in the app), or the run files given (`runs`, which is how an HTTP or MCP caller lists the files it kept). For each run: whether its seal holds, its id, how many hypotheses it registered and how many are supported, not supported or without evidence, how many a resume would run, how many inputs it pins, and what resuming would do. A file whose seal fails is listed as refused with the reason, never dropped. Hand one to research_run_status for its decisions, or to resume_research_run.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

runs.description: the run files to list; in the app, left unset, the research runs this project holds.

name: list_research_runs

count.description: how many runs opened under their seal

refused.description: each file whose seal failed, by position, with the reason

runs.description: one row per run whose seal holds: id, hypotheses, supported, not supported, without evidence, pending, settled, canceled, inputs pinned and the next action
